To check them I read the definitions they rely on: `cubicThetaPrimeCubeBranchPoint` (BranchCoordinates), `cubicThetaPrimeCubeBottomFunctionSum` (FourierOperator), `cubicThetaHorizontalPeriodization`/`Fraction` (HorizontalPeriodization), `cubicThetaHorizontalPeriodization_mean` (HorizontalPeriodMean), `cubicThetaHorizontalPoint`/`cubicThetaSectionHorizontal`/`_periodic` (HorizontalSection) and `CubicThetaSection` (AutomorphicSections). I also read the downstream uses in BranchFourier and HorizontalMean.

- `cubicThetaPrimeCubeBottomBranch_point` is a pointwise coordinate identity and is already as general as the definitions allow.
- `cubicThetaPrimeCubeBottom_periodization` restricts to automorphic sections with no need. This is reported below.
- `cubicThetaPrimeCubeBottom_mean` really does use the section structure. Automorphy gives horizontal periodicity, and `cubicThetaHorizontalPeriodization_mean` needs that periodicity plus continuity. One could generalise it to any continuous function on `CubicThetaPoint` with a horizontal-periodicity hypothesis. That would add a hypothesis and only repackage the existing `cubicThetaHorizontalPeriodization_mean`, so I did not report it.
- The `primaryPrime p` hypothesis is used here only for `p ≠ 0`. It is required by the upstream definitions (`cubicThetaPrimeCubeBranchPoint`, `cubicThetaPrimeCubeBottomFunctionSum`), so weakening it would mean changing other files. I did not report it.

findings.problem: The lemma takes an automorphic section `F : CubicThetaSection` but only uses `F.val` as a plain function. The proof unfolds `cubicThetaPrimeCubeBottomFunctionSum` and `cubicThetaHorizontalPeriodization`, uses `tsum_congr`, rewrites each term with the pointwise identity `cubicThetaPrimeCubeBottomBranch_point`, and closes with `rfl`. Neither automorphy nor continuity is used. Meanwhile `cubicThetaPrimeCubeBottomFunctionSum` is defined for any `F : CubicThetaPoint → ℂ`, and `cubicThetaHorizontalPeriodization` for any `f : ℂ → ℂ`. The operator is already applied to non-section inputs: `cubicThetaPrimeCubeBottomFunctionSum_mode` applies it to `cubicThetaPrimeCubeFourierMode h f`. So this rewrite is artificially limited to sections.
findings.proposed_change:
Restate it for an arbitrary function. Keep the section version as a one-line corollary if the `C(ℂ,ℂ)` form on the right is convenient downstream:

lemma cubicThetaPrimeCubeBottom_periodization {p : Eisenstein} (hp : primaryPrime p)
    (F : CubicThetaPoint → ℂ) (v : ℝ) (hv : 0<v) (z : ℂ) :
    cubicThetaPrimeCubeBottomFunctionSum hp F (cubicThetaHorizontalPoint v hv z)=
      cubicThetaHorizontalPeriodization (p^3)
        (fun w => F (cubicThetaHorizontalPoint (v/‖(p:ℂ)‖^3)
          (div_pos hv (pow_pos (norm_pos_iff.mpr (fun he => hp.2.ne_zero (Subtype.ext he))) 3)) w)) z := by
  unfold cubicThetaPrimeCubeBottomFunctionSum cubicThetaHorizontalPeriodization
  apply tsum_congr
  intro r
  rw [cubicThetaPrimeCubeBottomBranch_point]
  rfl

The proof is the existing one. The final `rfl` now only has to unfold `cubicThetaHorizontalFraction`, with no `ContinuousMap` coercion involved. The current section version, used in `cubicThetaPrimeCubeBottom_mean` and `cubicThetaPrimeCubeBottom_fourier`, follows as `cubicThetaPrimeCubeBottom_periodization hp F.val v hv z`. This holds because `cubicThetaSectionHorizontal F v hv` is defined as `⟨fun z => F.val (cubicThetaHorizontalPoint v hv z), _⟩`, so its coercion reduces definitionally to the same function. There are no degenerate cases: the statement is pointwise and holds for every function, and `p ≠ 0` comes from `hp` exactly as before.
findings.benefit: Users can rewrite the bottom Hecke branch as an explicit horizontal periodization for any test function, such as a single Fourier mode or a non-automorphic cutoff, without first building an automorphic section. The statement also makes clear that this step is pure coordinate bookkeeping. Automorphy is needed only in the mean and Fourier lemmas, through `cubicThetaSectionHorizontal_periodic`.
